Foundation: the Git boundary. Trail #494. New worktree wp-git-boundary off fresh origin/main. Read ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/architecture/ for git and release, docs/adr/README.md (Git access decisions), crates/callisto-model/src/vcs/ (GitAccess, boundary.rs Pathspec) and the ledger rows in /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/plans/FINDINGS-LEDGER.md. Today remote access has no model: callisto-graph reads git remote get-url --push origin and parses/rewrites it with url::Url (release/binding.rs ~151-290), then runs ls-remote and push against that rewritten URL (release/local.rs ~116, commands/init.rs ~940, release/provider/tag.rs), while the default branch is read by remote name (init.rs ~788, ~805). Build, in the vcs boundary of callisto-model (MIT; no FSL deps; concrete types, no new traits; CommandRunner stays the only seam): (1) GitRemote: every remote operation (ls-remote of tags, push of tags, default branch) invokes git with the remote NAME so git resolves it exactly once; the binding between plan and execution is a fingerprint (digest) of git's own outputs of git remote get-url <name> and get-url --push <name>, rechecked before each effect; a separate pure classification yields the GitHub owner/repo only for forge features and is never passed to git; the raw URL is never Display/Debug-printable. Remove the url::Url parsing and rewriting of remotes and the not-hosted refusals that existed only because Callisto built URLs itself; keep refusing what is a real policy (for example credentials embedded in the URL being recorded anywhere) and say which you kept and why. (2) Rev: revisions passed to git are built only from a CommitSha or a fully qualified ref (refs/tags/<name>, refs/heads/<name>), passed after --end-of-options where git supports it; migrate read_at, commit_time, resolve_commit, path_exists_at, files_containing_at, commits_since and their callers. (3) One GitPath for literal paths (merge Pathspec::literal and the check-ignore './' helper). (4) Move the direct git add calls (callisto-graph apply.rs ~654, callisto-cli commands/pre.rs ~21) into GitAccess. (5) One git environment policy applied by the boundary to every call: no prompts (GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0), output we parse is not affected by user config (no color, no pager, core.quotepath=false, a fixed locale where output is parsed); verify what exists today first and say what changed. Migrate every caller; delete the old paths (AGENTS: a PR that replaces an API deletes the old one). Tests against real git for: insteadOf and pushInsteadOf on scp and https forms, a separate pushurl, local-path and file:// remotes, a remote named other than origin if supported, a tag named like an option (-x) or with revision syntax, paths with leading ':' '-' and newlines. # Architecture decision records

- [1. Changesets-compatible change records](0001-changesets-compatible-change-records.md) — `.changeset/*.md` in `@changesets/cli`'s format, commit inference opt-in; guardrail: do not make Conventional Commits the primary input or change the file format without a new ADR.
- [2. The committed version decision is the release authority](0002-committed-decision-is-release-authority.md) — CI verifies the merged commit against the decision `callisto version --emit-decision` committed; guardrail: do not re-derive cascade or group policy after merge without a new ADR.
- [3. Reruns observe and adopt landed effects; no persisted execution state](0003-reruns-adopt-landed-effects.md) — every run observes providers and adopts what landed, state stays in memory; guardrail: do not add a persisted execution state file or recovery commands without a new ADR.
- [4. Ecosystem tools publish and own authentication](0004-ecosystem-tools-publish-and-own-auth.md) — `cargo`, the npm-family tools, `twine` and `gh` publish with their own credentials; guardrail: do not add native registry clients or a credential pre-flight without a new ADR.
- [5. System git only](0005-system-git-only.md) — every Git command in the `callisto` binary runs the system `git`; guardrail: do not add gix or a second Git backend without a new ADR.
- [6. moon integrates through a proto plugin, not a WASM extension](0006-moon-through-proto-plugin-not-wasm-extension.md) — moon users install the native CLI with a proto TOML plugin; guardrail: do not add a moon WASM extension or WASM build without a new ADR.
- [7. Platform packages are owned through optionalDependencies and release with their owner](0007-platform-packages-owned-through-optional-dependencies.md) — an `os`+`cpu` package with one owner releases with that owner; guardrail: do not require fixed-group entries or explicit config for platform packages without a new ADR.
- [8. Format-preserving manifest writes gated by ApplyPermit](0008-format-preserving-writes-gated-by-apply-permit.md) — `toml_edit` and fingerprinted JSON through `atomic_write(&ApplyPermit)`; guardrail: do not use typed serde round-trips for TOML, unfingerprinted `package.json` rewrites, regex edits or unpermitted writes without a new ADR.
- [9. A tag's identity is its commit and being annotated](0009-tag-identity-is-commit-and-annotation.md) — an existing annotated tag on the planned commit is adopted whatever its message; guardrail: do not compare annotation text or accept lightweight tags without a new ADR.
- [10. The workspace resolves natively after `version` or `snapshot`](0010-native-resolution-after-version.md) — a co-released dependent's spec is always raised to the new version and lockfiles refresh by default; guardrail: do not go back to rewriting only out-of-range specs or make lockfile refresh opt-in without a new ADR.
- [11. Directory-keyed packages and promotion-aware history](0011-directory-keyed-package-identity.md) — the directory key survives display promotion; new default tags use the promoted display id and historical bare records use an ownership fallback; guardrail: do not derive paths or persisted keys from the display id without a new ADR.
- [12. Canonical distribution references and explicit release ownership](0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md) — accepted v1 model. Separates native distribution identities, version authority and shared effects while preserving deliberate historical migration.
- [13. An interrupted `version` run resumes from its recorded inputs](0013-interrupted-version-runs-resume-from-a-checkpoint-ref.md) — proposed. `version` records its inputs at `refs/callisto/checkpoint/version` before writing; guardrail: do not restore written files in process or persist the plan without a new ADR.

## Rules

- An ADR records an architecturally significant decision that had a credible alternative.
- `Proposed` until the PR that implements it merges, then `Accepted`.
- A changed decision gets a new ADR with `Status: Supersedes N`. The old file moves to `docs/adr/superseded/` with `Status: Superseded by M`. Agents do not load that folder.
- Every reason cites a source (commit, PR, historical doc). If none exists, write "Reason not recorded".
- Behaviour belongs in `docs/specs/`; coding rules belong in `AGENTS.md`.

# 5. System git only

Status: Accepted (implemented in #145)

## Context

- Callisto reads commits, tags and staged changes, and creates and pushes tags.
- From 2026-08-03 `callisto-vcs` had two backends behind `GitDataSource`: native gix (`GitRepository`) and a shell fallback (`ShellGit`), with reads retrying through the shell on any native error (commit bb2a69cc4).
- The CLI already required a `git` binary: trust observation, staged changes and every fallback went through it (#145).

## Decision

Every Git command in the `callisto` binary runs the user's `git` through `CommandRunner`. `callisto_model::vcs` has one Git access type, `GitAccess`, and defines no backend trait; `GitAccess` implements callisto-model's `CommitWalker` for severity inference (`crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs`). Git operations use the user's git config and identity, except release tags: with no identity set, the target commit's committer becomes the tagger, and `TagSignPolicy::ForceUnsigned` adds `--no-sign` (`crates/callisto-vcs/src/access.rs`). Workspace-root discovery looks for a `.git` entry on disk (`crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/root.rs`).

## Options considered

- **gix as the primary backend with a shell fallback (two backends)** — rejected in #145: "Two backends meant two semantics to keep in step (gix ignored TagSignPolicy) and 106 extra crates." The changeset adds: "every Git read and write already had to work through the `git` binary the CLI requires."
- **gix only** — not considered in #145. Reason not recorded.

## Consequences

- History walks use `git log --no-merges --full-history`, matching the gix commit sets; plain `git log` history simplification drops commits whose change a later merge discarded.
- Callisto depends on the installed git version and parses its output.
- Annotated tags work on runners with no git identity: the tagger falls back to the target commit's committer (#145).
- The managed release-PR action is outside this decision: it writes its commit and branch refs through the GitHub API (`.github/actions/callisto-action/scripts/create-or-update-release-pr.sh`).
- Today `release-pr commit-plan` reads staged bytes from the worktree, not the index (as of 0.10.2; `git show 07154021c:docs/projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md`, v1 fix plan §1).

## Enforcement

- `callisto_model::vcs` has no gix dependency and one `GitAccess` type (`crates/callisto-model/src/vcs/access.rs`).
- Nothing bans gix in `deny.toml`; reintroducing it needs a new ADR.

- A required Git operation is impossible or unacceptably slow through the binary, measured against the #145 numbers.
- Callisto must run where no `git` binary exists.

# Release execution

The types that make a release run safe to crash and rerun, and how the two release routes share them. Behavior: [`docs/specs/release.json`](../specs/release.json). Operator guide: [`docs/releasing.md`](../releasing.md). Decisions: ADRs [2](../adr/0002-committed-decision-is-release-authority.md), [3](../adr/0003-reruns-adopt-landed-effects.md), [4](../adr/0004-ecosystem-tools-publish-and-own-auth.md) and [7](../adr/0007-platform-packages-owned-through-optional-dependencies.md).

## Terms

- Package: a dependency-graph node owned by a directory; it can expose several canonical manifest/distribution identities.
- Distribution identity: `ReleasePackageId`, an ecosystem-qualified native package name. A graph package with several identities has one tag, one forge release and one forge publish, each carried by the package's owner: its first selected identity in manifest order (Cargo, then npm, then PyPI).
- Artifact: the bytes of one *(package, version, target)*, declared by `[release] targets` with an `asset-name` template or by `[[release.artifact]]`. It has no version, tag or changelog of its own. Callisto does not parse `target`; CI supplies product-slot bytes and Callisto records where they go. Registry publishing can invoke native build/pack tools: Python's build backend and each npm package manager's `pack`.
- Product package: `[release].product-package`. Every artifact slot uploads to the product's one GitHub Release, even when another package built the bytes (`ArtifactSlotId.package`).
- Decision: the package and version roster (`ReleaseDecisionV1`).
- Intent: the decision plus the source snapshot, every operation with its prerequisites, and the artifact slots, sealed by a digest (`ReleaseIntentV1`).
- Operation: one effect on one provider, identified by package, version and role: registry publish, platform publish, tag, forge release (draft), artifact upload, forge publish. The operations form a DAG by prerequisite; `callisto_model::canonical_operation_order`, built on `michi-graph`, validates it (a cycle is reported as one operation on it) and fixes the order: the smallest topological order by operation id.

| Derivation and execution | `callisto-graph` | Decisions (`commands/release_decision.rs`), intent derivation (`commands/release/derive.rs`), local route (`commands/release/local.rs`), executor (`commands/release_execution.rs`), provider adapters (`commands/release/provider/`) |

## Two routes, one executor

```
local:  derive_release_roster (untagged versions, plus tagged-on-HEAD releases not fully observed)  -> plan_loaded_release -> intent
CI:     committed decision file, or --package over plan_version -> release plan -> intent -> build -> release execute
both:   intent -> ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1::new -> execute_release -> ReleaseReceiptV1::from_state
```

- `plan_loaded_release` is the one derivation behind both `callisto release --dry-run` and the real run.
- A tag proves only that the tag was created. `incomplete_tagged_releases` observes every operation of the packages tagged on HEAD and keeps any not exactly satisfied; a tag on another commit is never observed.
- `ci_release_route` sends a workspace with artifact slots or platform builds to the CI route before anything runs.
- `expand_selection` (group members) and `require_dependencies_selected` (unselected unreleased dependencies) apply to both routes.

## Managed release PR and workflow

Callisto's own [release workflow](../../.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml) reconstructs one `callisto/version-packages` PR from `main` whenever the version plan versions a package: a pending changeset, or commits a package with `release-trigger = "auto"` infers a bump from. It versions manifests and changelogs; merging the PR consumes the changesets on `main` and authorizes publication.

- The action commits non-workflow changes through `createCommitOnBranch`, then moves the release ref through REST. It does not run a local `git push`. Workflow files remain unchanged, so the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` needs no workflow-write permission.
- Commits are GitHub-signed as `github-actions[bot]`. An App or fine-grained token can use another identity.
- Branch protection must require reviews and CI checks. CODEOWNERS alone does not enforce review.
- The PR body is composed after the version command, from the `ReleasePreview` it wrote (`version --emit-preview`), because that command consumes the changesets the body describes. `compose-pr-body --preview --publish-plan` also plans the versioned tree's release offline, so "Merging will publish" names only targets the release derives from the same decision, and a plan the release would refuse leads the body with a caution. Registry-side checks stay with the release. The same report lists the labels Callisto manages (`callisto: ready|blocked|breaking|action-required|unreleased-changes`, `bump: major|minor|patch`) each with an `applied` flag derived from the preview's findings, so the action adds, creates and removes labels without naming any. See [versioning](versioning.md).
- `version-pr` maintains the PR; `release` runs the local release route and `execute` runs `callisto release execute` on a prepared handoff. Generated workflows use package/execute (simple) or plan/build/attest/pack/execute (build-matrix). The [action manifest](../../.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml) defines current inputs and outputs.
- Each main run asks `callisto release pending` for the oldest merged release commit whose tags or GitHub release are missing, validates its merge SHA on main history, and releases it with current orchestration. After execution succeeds, the workflow dispatches the next unfinished release, and refreshes the managed PR once none remains. Nothing is recorded on the PR; the committed decision and provider observations remain release authority.
- Only `execute` receives registry credentials. Plan, build, attest and pack jobs receive none. Temporary intent, receipt, artifacts, and build output live under `RUNNER_TEMP`, outside the checkout.

## Publish isolation

A job either sees project source and runs project code, or holds registry secrets or an OIDC token. Never both, except `execute`, which checks out the source only for the tag push and the cargo publish and runs no build or package-manager script.

- Build and pack jobs hold read-only permissions and no secret. Python distributions are built by `release build-python` and npm tarballs packed by `release pack-npm` (the workspace's own packer, so `workspace:` ranges are rewritten), each into a directory a later job downloads.
- Attestation is its own job with no checkout and no `run` step, because it holds `id-token: write`.
- `release artifact-manifest --seal-python --seal-npm` records each file's name, size and sha256 in the manifest, so the run envelope's manifest digest covers them. `execute` verifies the bytes, then publishes exactly those files: `twine upload <files>` and `npm publish <tarball> --ignore-scripts`.
- On the CI route, a plan with an npm or PyPI publish needs a manifest that seals each of them: none, or one that misses a publish, fails (E306) when the manifest is verified, before any effect, and again before the publish command, so the fallback is never a build or pack beside the credentials. The local route has no manifest: it packs or builds in a temporary directory with credentials withheld, then publishes the same way.
- `prepack` and `prepare` run in the pack job; `prepublishOnly`, `publish` and `postpublish` do not run. The CI route publishes crates with `cargo publish --no-verify`: a credential-free job first runs `release package-cargo`, which compiles every crate of the release with one `cargo package --locked -p a -p b` call per owning Cargo workspace, run from that workspace's directory (one call per workspace because a lone crate cannot resolve an unpublished sibling of the same release, and a layout such as `native/Cargo.toml` with no root manifest has no workspace at the checkout root), and the job graph, with `execute` needing that job, is the record. The local route keeps cargo's own verification.

GitHub Actions schedules jobs, transports artifacts, and injects credentials. Callisto validates source, provenance, plan, observations, transitions, terminality, receipts, and artifacts. Workflow shell must not reimplement those semantics. Recovery dispatch uses current orchestration on `main` with an explicit merged source SHA and runs credential-free `recovery-checks` instead of full `verify`. Planning and building run alongside the gate (`verify` or `recovery-checks`); `execute` and the release PR refresh wait for the `gate` job, so nothing is published or refreshed unless verification passed.

The generated release action (`mode: release`, or `mode: execute` on a handoff directory) maps credentials; no package script runs during the publish:

- npm: copy existing user config to a mode-0600 temporary file, add an npmjs entry interpolating `NPM_TOKEN`, point `npm` at it, and remove it on exit. The original config is unchanged. `NPM_TOKEN` remains available for `.npmrc` interpolation. Custom registries use native configuration. Only `npm` publishes, whichever package manager packed the tarball, so no pnpm, yarn or bun auth is mapped, and a registry set only in a yarn workspace's `.yarnrc.yml` or a bun workspace's `bunfig.toml` is refused (E168) when the intent is derived, because `npm publish <tarball>` would not honor it.
- PyPI: map `PYPI_TOKEN` to `TWINE_USERNAME=__token__` and `TWINE_PASSWORD` for upload. The build backend receives no registry or forge credentials.
- Cargo: pass `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` through to Cargo.

The CLI runner also passes `CARGO_REGISTRIES_*_TOKEN` only to Cargo. Other child processes receive neither the default nor named Cargo registry tokens.

## Run envelope and state (`release/execution.rs`)

- `ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1` is one run's identity: orchestration revision, release-source revision, intent digest, artifact-manifest digest.
- `ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1::new` is its only constructor. The source revision and intent digest are read from the intent, so a caller cannot assert them; the constructor cross-checks the rest against the intent before any effect.
- `ReleaseExecutionStateV1::new(intent, envelope)` is the only way to start a state, so no state exists without a validated envelope.
- The state is never persisted or loaded. Every run starts with every operation `Pending`.
- `ReleaseReceiptV1::from_state` builds the receipt from the state alone: the envelope plus the evidence each operation recorded on success. Nothing re-observes providers after the effects.

## Observation and evidence (`release_observation.rs`)

- `ProviderObservationV1` is `Absent`, `Exact { evidence }`, `Conflict { reason }` or `Indeterminate { cause }`. Reasons and causes are closed enums.
- `ProviderEvidenceV1` is closed and per role: registry version, git tag peeled commit, forge release tag and draft flag, artifact size and sha256.
- `ReleaseOperationObservationV1::new` rejects evidence whose shape does not belong to the operation's role; deserialization goes through it too.
- Proof tokens: `AbsentProof` is minted only from `Absent`, `ExactEvidence` only from `Exact`.
- `execute_release` observes each operation once before its effect: exact is adopted, absent is performed then confirmed, anything else stops the run before the effect.
- An npm registry publish is the exception to "then confirmed": it is issued, stays `Attempting`, and another npm publish may follow it. When nothing else can start, the executor looks at all issued publishes together until each is shown or the longest `confirm-timeout` is spent. That window is one `ConfirmationWave`: it opens when the first publish is issued, is measured on the provider set's clock so looking counts, and a publish shown along the way does not restart it. Each look is given the window that is left as its patience, so a registry that asks for long waits between tries cannot hold a look past the window; a look that has none left tries once. The tag, release draft, uploads and publication wait for the confirmation, so nothing is announced before the registry shows the version. Cargo and PyPI publishes are confirmed as they are published (PyPI completion is a file set, not a version).

Provider reads use native tools for Cargo and npm, and `curl` for PyPI's PEP 691 JSON simple index:

- Cargo: `cargo info NAME@VERSION --registry REGISTRY` runs from the source root. Matching `version:` means exact; exit 101 with ``could not find `NAME@VERSION` `` means absent. Other results are indeterminate. Yanked versions are invisible to `cargo info`; a rejected publish ends without a receipt.
- npm: `npm view NAME@VERSION --json --fetch-retries=0`, run in the workspace that owns the package, as the publish is.
- PyPI: a matching file means exact; 404 or no match means absent; transport failure or non-JSON means indeterminate. Yanked matches count as absent. Before an effect, `release execute` also builds the release's files once into a temporary directory and compares their names with the index, so a partly uploaded release uploads only what is missing and is satisfied only when the whole set is there.

Adopting a version that is already published is by design, so a rerun can finish a half-done release. Because a foreign package would be adopted the same way, a Cargo or npm adoption also reads the repository the registry records for that version (`repository:` in `cargo info`, `repository` in `npm view`) and warns, without blocking, when it names a different repository from `origin`. A registry that records none, or a failed read, says nothing; PyPI's simple index records no repository, so it is not checked.

Planning looks at many packages at once, so its reads are built to scale with the number of packages, not to add a process or a round trip per package:

- Observations that the plan makes before any effect (the published-version check, the name check, the resumable-release check) are independent reads and run side by side, up to eight at a time, in package order.
- The name check is advisory, so it waits at most one second between its own tries and says nothing when a registry does not answer; the checks a release depends on keep the full retry schedule. An unreachable network therefore costs a preview seconds, not a minute.
- Git history for all packages is read in batches (one `cat-file --batch` for manifests, one for each package's candidate version commit and its parent, one `cat-file --batch-check` that compares package directories by tree id), plus one `git log` per package.
- The workspace is loaded once per command, and the one `git ls-remote` that finds tags missing from `origin` runs beside planning.
- `just bench` reports wall time and git process counts per command; a change that adds a git process per package fails review.

These reads are version-level checks, not proof of identical bytes or the npm dist-tag. Registry endpoints must be HTTPS. Read-only observations before an effect retry 429, 5xx, rate-limited 403, and transport failures with backoff and `Retry-After`. Effects are never blindly retried; outbound commands have deadlines.

After a registry publish the version may not be readable yet: npm serves a package's document with `max-age=300`, a missing package's 404 included, so a read just before the publish can answer stale for five minutes. The confirmation therefore waits by time, not tries, treating absent and unreachable as lag until the registry's window (`confirm-timeout`, default 6 minutes for npm and PyPI, 2 for Cargo) is spent, then fails with E157. An exact version or a conflict ends the wait at once.

## Transition table (`release_transition.rs`)

`transition` is the only function that computes an `OperationState`; `ReleaseExecutionStateV1::apply` is the only mutator. The whole legal edge set:

| From | Event | To |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pending | `Attempt { AbsentProof }` | Attempting |
| Pending | `ObservedExactBeforeEffect { ExactEvidence }` | AlreadySatisfied |
| Attempting | `Confirmed { ExactEvidence }` | Published |
| Attempting | `EffectFailedAndAbsent { AbsentProof }` | Failed |
| Pending or Attempting | `Blocked { reason }` | Blocked |

- Any other pair is an `InvalidTransition`.
- `Attempting` is unreachable without a proof of absence.
- `Published` (our effect landed) stays distinct from `AlreadySatisfied` (it existed before this run).

## Forge ordering

- A GitHub release is created as a draft, assets upload to the draft, and publication is a separate last operation that depends on every upload. A published release can be immutable and refuse new assets.
- GitHub's release-by-tag endpoint omits drafts, so the forge lookup finds the release ID by tag through GraphQL, then reads the release by ID (`release/github.rs`).
- GitHub's reads lag its writes by seconds. The check right after this run's own create, upload or publish retries an absent answer for about a minute before it reports a conflict (`observe_until_visible`).

The tag/announcement barrier covers all required publications of a graph package: a package's tag waits for the registry publishes of every release identity it has (`OpIndex::tag_prerequisites`), so a dual Cargo/npm owner's one tag and public release follow both publishes, in no fixed ecosystem order. A dependency edge is not a barrier: it orders only the dependent's distribution in the declaring manifest's ecosystem (`link_publish_prerequisites`), so a dual owner's Cargo-only dependency holds its crate, not its npm package. Selecting one identity of a dual package releases every identity of that package, so the tag never waits on a subset of its publishes. A product's public release also waits for the tag, and so the registry publishes, of each other package whose asset it carries. An intent derived before either rule fails closed as stale and is rebuilt with `release plan`. See [the scoped design](polyglot-v1.md) for proposed ownership and future Go tag-publication semantics.

## Wire and observation boundaries

Stdout JSON reports include `schemaVersion`, `command` and `dryRun`; durable decision, intent, artifact-manifest and receipt files retain their own wire shapes. The CLI's `release-pr verify` reader accepts both the strict bare decision and unchanged decide report, validating the report metadata before passing the payload to the shared domain constructor. Unknown and duplicate fields remain errors; durable wire readers are unchanged. The real-binary action contract exercises this producer/consumer boundary through inline, file and stdin inputs.

Managed PR verification compares the original snapshot before staging and before moving the release ref. After a successful update, the action confirms the ref's exact new SHA and supplies it as `--applied-head` for the final check. The model validates the original update decision and allows only its selected PR's head to change to that SHA; the base, repository, PR roster and every other head remain unchanged. Create decisions keep strict equality until the PR is created. The action does not rewrite its decision or discard concurrency checks after its own effect.

Registry evidence currently confirms a version, with optional checksum/yank fields; it does not establish byte identity. npm publishes the sealed tarball only, and a manifest that seals an npm publish records one set per published npm package (a platform package under its own name), each exactly one file named as `npm pack` names it; the adapter rechecks the digest before `npm publish`, and a rerun adopts a version the registry already shows, so the tarball path is re-derived from the manifest each run and nothing is recorded. Python completion has two modes. Without a sealed file set (the local route, and a CI route whose manifest seals none) it is judged against the files the executing run builds, matched by name, and digests are compared only for files that run uploaded: a rebuild need not be byte-identical to an earlier attempt. With a sealed set, a build job (`release build-python`, no credentials) builds the files and `release artifact-manifest --seal-python` records each file's name, size and sha256 in the manifest, so the envelope's manifest digest covers them. `release execute` verifies the bytes, builds nothing, uploads those files, and treats any index file under a sealed name with another sha256 as an error (E307). The sealed sets are all or none per ecosystem and each belongs to a Python or npm publish of the intent; the manifest stays at schema version 1 because a manifest without sets is unchanged and an older reader rejects the new field. Artifact size/sha256 validation otherwise applies to declared GitHub assets. A PyPI registry reads its simple index at `url` and uploads to `publish-url` when set, else `url`; both endpoints are part of the registry binding. Authenticated reads and HTML-only indexes are not supported.

## Verification tiers

- Fault-injection simulator (`commands/release_simulator.rs`): drives the real `execute_release` against an in-memory provider world, crashing at every provider call and injecting every provider outcome, with each rerun starting fresh. It asserts that a receipt is issued only when every effect really landed and only from state, that no landed effect is re-issued, that no effect lands before its prerequisites, and that each scenario converges within three clean reruns.
- Provider contract tier: fake providers replay captured real responses from `testing/fixtures/providers/`; `TOOL_SHAPES` in `crates/callisto-cli/tests/common/release_harness.rs` rejects flags a fake does not know, and `provider_flag_contract_tests.rs` checks each emitted flag against the real tool. `just provider-fixtures` re-captures and `just provider-contract` checks shapes live; both need the network and are outside `just ci`.
- Wire shapes: decision, intent, envelope and receipt each carry a `SCHEMA_VERSION`; the execution state has no wire shape. `callisto schema --type release-receipt` publishes the receipt schema, guarded by `crates/callisto-cli/tests/schema_guard_test.rs`.

## Installer and product assets

`setup-callisto` defaults to `source: auto`: install the requested release, even in a Callisto checkout. An explicit `version` wins; otherwise `latest` resolves the pinned action ref to its `callisto@` release when possible. A `callisto-cli` manifest alone does not select checkout source.

`source: local` builds the checkout and ignores `version`. It requires tracked root and CLI manifests, the CLI entrypoint, a Cargo-confirmed workspace member and binary target, Git, Cargo, jq, and locked offline metadata resolution. It uses the checkout's `target/` cache, installs under `RUNNER_TEMP`, and never falls back from invalid local source. Callisto's release jobs use this mode.

`setup-callisto` downloads the release archive and checks it with `gh attestation verify` against `orin-dx/callisto`, the `callisto-release.yml` signer and the `refs/heads/main` source ref before extraction; only the `callisto` binary is extracted. There is no opt-out and no crates.io fallback, so generated workflows never run an unverified binary in the `execute` job. The `version` input is `latest`, a bare version (`0.21.0`, read as `callisto@0.21.0`) or a `callisto@` tag; anything else fails before any download. A missing platform asset (HTTP 404), a failed verification and a missing `gh` each fail the step with a link to [install in CI](../install-in-ci.md), which gives the manual steps for other environments; any other download failure after the retries asks to retry the job. Only network and HTTP errors on the download are retried, never a verification failure.

Product assets target `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, and `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`. The Intel macOS asset is cross-compiled on an Apple silicon runner, and the arm64 Linux asset is built natively on an arm64 runner. Apple signing and notarization are out of scope. GitHub provenance binds assets to the orchestration revision; the intent and artifact manifest bind their bytes to the release source. Callisto publishes its crates to crates.io and product assets to GitHub Releases, not to another registry for rehearsal.

`just test-real-tools` rehearses recovery against local registries through the production registry binding, with no test-only allowance in the https rule: Verdaccio, `pypiserver` and a JSON simple index serve a self-signed loopback certificate that npm, curl and Twine trust through their own CA variables. The rehearsals are a partial npm publish adopted by a rerun, a PyPI index that shows an upload late or never, a remote tag on another commit, and a PyPI release whose index lacks one built file. Cargo is rehearsed through a `kind = "cargo"` registry named in `publish-to`: a local sparse registry with the publish and download API stands behind `[registries.<name>] index` in a scratch `CARGO_HOME`, and callisto passes `--registry <name>` to `cargo publish` and `cargo info`. The Cargo registry is plain `http` on loopback because callisto never sees its URL, so no https rule applies to it. The Cargo rehearsals are a partial publish adopted by a rerun, an index that shows a publish late (cargo itself does not wait), and a remote tag on another commit. A `crates-io` publish runs plain `cargo publish`, so it is not rehearsed against a local registry.

`just test-real-tools` also runs the real `@changesets/cli` 3.x and 2.x beside callisto in scratch npm workspaces and compares versions. One scenario plans a fixed group in Changesets, runs `callisto init`, and expects the same packages and versions from `callisto version --dry-run`; the other enters a pre cycle with Changesets, then expects callisto to give the next beta and the exit release Changesets itself gives. `init` does not translate `fixed`, so the first scenario adds the `[[fixed-group]]` the `init` warning names. Changesets 3.x `init` asks questions on a TTY, so only 2.x runs it; 3.x gets its default config written.

`just test-real-tools` then runs `native_resolution_e2e_tests` and fails when `npm`, `pnpm` or `uv` is missing, so the matrix is recorded rather than skipped. After `version` or `snapshot` each ecosystem's own locked install must still succeed:

| Ecosystem | Command | Checked after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cargo | `cargo metadata --locked --offline` | `version`, `snapshot` |
| npm | `npm ci` | `version`, `snapshot` |
| pnpm | `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` | `version`, `snapshot`, lockfile refresh |
| pnpm | `pnpm pack` with `workspace:` protocols rewritten to the released versions | `version`, `snapshot` |
| Python | `uv lock --check` | `version`, `snapshot` |
